candidates.comment: From the video I have learned that I would like to try the LM1875 because it is a more stable chip to the TDA2050. In the second video I watched it was a side-by-side comparison of the TDA2050 and the LM1875 to determine which chip was better. The first test was the power tests where he tested different voltages and calculated the watts that were running through the chip. The TDA2050 did better as the supply voltage increased. It was unclear what the reasoning for this test was he did not explain that very well in my opinion. The next test looking at the rail sticking. Rail sticking explained towards the end of the video is only an issue when you play the speakers loudly and you will hear clipping from the amplifier. The LM1875 did better than the TDA2050 which had a heavy rail stick. The next text was the frequency response test and both chips preformed the same. According to JohnAudioTech that is not so much of an issue due to the fact that it is more affected by the external components more than the chips. The next test he performed was the step response test. We looked at the square wave on the oscilloscope. When looking at the LM1875 there was some overshoot and at different signal levels with different capacitance amounts as he raises the capacitance, we see the ringing increase to the point where an oscillation occurs. A ring is a dampened oscillation. With the LM1875 the chip was mostly stable with only light oscillations, when he tested the TDA2050 the chip was very unstable where he had to use a what he called a Thiele network. The next test was the distortion test first he tested the TDA2050, and it showed low distortion whereas the LM1875 showed a higher distortion which he found surprising based on the stability of the step tests. The intermodulation distortion was higher for the LM1875 than for the TDA2050. Although there were no tests for the current limiter, he used his previous knowledge and he said that the TDA2050’s current limiter was worse. I am curious to try the LM1875 chip know and see if we produce better results with that chip than we did with the TDA2050. I need to learn more about Thiele Networks and how to use them because it sounds like it might be something that will improve our sound quality with both chips and make it more stable for use. I have learned that we need to put heat sinks on our chips from this video. It will better protect the whole circuit. Some of the tests that were run I am still unsure what they were indicating and how to better apply that to the project. Below are the links for my videos since I was unable to get my zoom to work. I was confused by some of the tests he ran and why he was running them.
candidates.url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iKZ05QIN8mc&t=476s: TDA2050 vs LM1875 performance tests to see which is the BEST

In the second video I watched it was a side-by-side comparison of the TDA2050 and the LM1875 to determine which chip was better. The first test was the power tests where he tested different voltages and calculated the watts that were running through the chip. The TDA2050 did better as the supply voltage increased. It was unclear what the reasoning for this test was he did not explain that very well in my opinion. The next test looking at the rail sticking. Rail sticking explained towards the end of the video is only an issue when you play the speakers loudly and you will hear clipping from the amplifier. The LM1875 did better than the TDA2050 which had a heavy rail stick. The next text was the frequency response test and both chips preformed the same. According to JohnAudioTech that is not so much of an issue due to the fact that it is more affected by the external components more than the chips. The next test he performed was the step response test. We looked at the square wave on the oscilloscope. When looking at the LM1875 there was some overshoot and at different signal levels with different capacitance amounts as he raises the capacitance, we see the ringing increase to the point where an oscillation occurs. A ring is a dampened oscillation. With the LM1875 the chip was mostly stable with only light oscillations, when he tested the TDA2050 the chip was very unstable where he had to use a what he called a Thiele network. The next test was the distortion test first he tested the TDA2050, and it showed low distortion whereas the LM1875 showed a higher distortion which he found surprising based on the stability of the step tests. The intermodulation distortion was higher for the LM1875 than for the TDA2050. Although there were no tests for the current limiter, he used his previous knowledge and he said that the TDA2050’s current limiter was worse. I am curious to try the LM1875 chip know and see if we produce better results with that chip than we did with the TDA2050. I need to learn more about Thiele Networks and how to use them because it sounds like it might be something that will improve our sound quality with both chips and make it more stable for use. candidates.comment: From the video I have learned that I would like to try the LM1875 because it is a more stable chip to the TDA2050. In the second video I watched it was a side-by-side comparison of the TDA2050 and the LM1875 to determine which chip was better. The first test was the power tests where he tested different voltages and calculated the watts that were running through the chip. The TDA2050 did better as the supply voltage increased. It was unclear what the reasoning for this test was he did not explain that very well in my opinion. The next test looking at the rail sticking. Rail sticking explained towards the end of the video is only an issue when you play the speakers loudly and you will hear clipping from the amplifier. The LM1875 did better than the TDA2050 which had a heavy rail stick. The next text was the frequency response test and both chips preformed the same. According to JohnAudioTech that is not so much of an issue due to the fact that it is more affected by the external components more than the chips. The next test he performed was the step response test. We looked at the square wave on the oscilloscope. When looking at the LM1875 there was some overshoot and at different signal levels with different capacitance amounts as he raises the capacitance, we see the ringing increase to the point where an oscillation occurs. A ring is a dampened oscillation. With the LM1875 the chip was mostly stable with only light oscillations, when he tested the TDA2050 the chip was very unstable where he had to use a what he called a Thiele network. The next test was the distortion test first he tested the TDA2050, and it showed low distortion whereas the LM1875 showed a higher distortion which he found surprising based on the stability of the step tests. The intermodulation distortion was higher for the LM1875 than for the TDA2050. Although there were no tests for the current limiter, he used his previous knowledge and he said that the TDA2050’s current limiter was worse. I am curious to try the LM1875 chip know and see if we produce better results with that chip than we did with the TDA2050. I need to learn more about Thiele Networks and how to use them because it sounds like it might be something that will improve our sound quality with both chips and make it more stable for use. I have learned that we need to put heat sinks on our chips from this video. It will better protect the whole circuit. Some of the tests that were run I am still unsure what they were indicating and how to better apply that to the project. Below are the links for my videos since I was unable to get my zoom to work. I was confused by some of the tests he ran and why he was running them.

The LM1875 did better than the TDA2050 which had a heavy rail stick. The next text was the frequency response test and both chips preformed the same. According to JohnAudioTech that is not so much of an issue due to the fact that it is more affected by the external components more than the chips. The next test he performed was the step response test. We looked at the square wave on the oscilloscope. When looking at the LM1875 there was some overshoot and at different signal levels with different capacitance amounts as he raises the capacitance, we see the ringing increase to the point where an oscillation occurs. A ring is a dampened oscillation. With the LM1875 the chip was mostly stable with only light oscillations, when he tested the TDA2050 the chip was very unstable where he had to use a what he called a Thiele network. The next test was the distortion test first he tested the TDA2050, and it showed low distortion whereas the LM1875 showed a higher distortion which he found surprising based on the stability of the step tests.
